evidence.explanation: States that no disease-modifying therapy is available and identifies enzyme replacement therapy as the unmet need.

treatments/0.description: No disease-modifying therapy exists for MPS X. There is no approved or investigational enzyme replacement therapy, no substrate reduction therapy, and no reported use of hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. Management is orthopaedic care for progressive hip dysplasia and femoral head osteonecrosis, analgesia for joint pain, and physiotherapy. Because the disease is chondro-osseous and the reported burden is pain and disability rather than organ failure, the authors of the fourth-patient report explicitly identify enzyme replacement therapy development as the unmet need.

evidence.snippet: The diagnosis of MPS type X allows for tailored cardiac, ophthalmologic and audiological surveillance, and can inform genetic counseling.
evidence.explanation: States the clinical utility of the diagnosis, which is surveillance and counselling rather than treatment.

treatments/1.description: Once ARSK-related MPS is molecularly confirmed, targeted surveillance is warranted even in an asymptomatic child, because the cardiac and ocular involvement documented in the index family was found only on deliberate reverse phenotyping and was clinically silent. Surveillance also substantiates genetic counselling for the family.

open_questions/0.rationale: The mismatch is not a failure of the model to reproduce a subtle feature; it is close to an inversion. The mouse has the biochemistry without the skeletal pathology and a behavioural phenotype instead, while humans have the skeletal pathology with normal cognition. Because the storage burden in MPS X is small in both species, the human skeletal phenotype is unlikely to be a simple dose effect of accumulated substrate. A more plausible reading is that glucuronate-2-O-sulfation is differentially abundant on the specific chondroitin and dermatan sulfate chains that carry load in the human growth plate and epiphysis, so the same enzymatic block has a tissue-specific consequence in humans that it does not have in mice. Resolving this matters practically: the mouse is the only available model, and it lacks the outcome an enzyme replacement therapy would need to move.

evidence.snippet: Neuroblastoma (NB) is a pediatric solid tumor originating from neural crest cells (NCCs), which are precursors of the sympathetic nervous system.
evidence.explanation: This abstract states neuroblastoma originates from neural crest cells, supporting the developmental origin described. Sourced from an iPSC-derived neural crest model transplanted into immunodeficient mice, not from patient material.

evidence.snippet: Neuroblastoma is a clinically heterogenous pediatric cancer of the sympathetic nervous system that originates from neural crest cells.
evidence.explanation: Supports neural crest origin and clinical heterogeneity of neuroblastoma.

steps/0.description: Neuroblastoma arises from neural crest-derived sympathoadrenal progenitor cells that fail to complete differentiation. The tumor cells retain characteristics of immature neuroblasts with variable capacity for sympathetic neuronal differentiation.

evidence.snippet: Anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) alterations, including mutations and amplification, activate oncogenic signaling pathways that, together with MYCN amplification, further enhance tumor malignancy.
evidence.explanation: Establishes ALK alterations (mutations and amplification) as activators of oncogenic signaling that synergize with MYCN to drive neuroblastoma malignancy.

evidence.snippet: Mutations resulted in constitutive phosphorylation, and targeted knockdown of ALK messenger RNA resulted in profound inhibition of growth in all cell lines harbouring mutant or amplified ALK
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates that ALK mutations cause constitutive receptor phosphorylation and that ALK-altered neuroblastoma cells are dependent on ALK for growth, supporting the causal edge into proliferation.

steps/1.description: ALK (anaplastic lymphoma kinase) is activated by point mutations in approximately 8-10% of neuroblastomas, and by amplification in additional cases. ALK mutations are enriched in familial neuroblastoma and represent a therapeutic target for ALK inhibitors.

evidence.snippet: MYCN amplification is a key factor contributing to the poor prognosis of NB.
evidence.explanation: Supports MYCN amplification as a driver of aggressive biology, but from an iPSC-derived neural crest model; the human clinical support for the prognostic half of the claim is the Brodeur item below.

evidence.snippet: Furthermore, N-myc amplification is highly correlated with advanced stages of disease (P less than 0.001) and with the ability to grow in vitro as an established cell line, both of which are associated with a poor prognosis.
evidence.explanation: Human clinical support for the aggressive-phenotype and poor-prognosis claim: in untreated primary tumors, MYCN amplification was absent in all 15 stage 1-2 cases and present in 50% of stage 3-4 cases.

steps/2.description: MYCN amplification results in massive overexpression of the MYCN transcription factor, a key contributor to aggressive neuroblastoma biology and poor prognosis. MYCN-amplified tumors have a distinct aggressive phenotype with rapid growth and early metastasis.

evidence.snippet: Anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) alterations, including mutations and amplification, activate oncogenic signaling pathways that, together with MYCN amplification, further enhance tumor malignancy.
evidence.explanation: Supports co-operation between ALK signalling and MYCN in driving malignancy. Marked PARTIAL and INDIRECT because the intervening signalling steps between ALK activation and the MYCN-driven proliferative program are not enumerated in the cited work.

edges/1.description: Constitutive ALK kinase signalling converges on the same proliferative output as MYCN amplification and co-operates with it; ALK-mutant and MYCN-amplified disease frequently co-occur and jointly enhance malignancy.

evidence.snippet: Stage, age, histologic category, grade of tumor differentiation, the status of the MYCN oncogene, chromosome 11q status, and DNA ploidy were the most highly statistically significant and clinically relevant factors.
evidence.explanation: The INRG Task Force analysis of 8,800 patients establishes MYCN status as one of the most statistically significant prognostic factors, and places it alongside (not above) stage, age, histology, 11q status, and ploidy in risk classification.

evidence.snippet: N-myc amplification is highly correlated with advanced stages of disease
evidence.explanation: The original Brodeur series in untreated primary tumors established the association of MYCN amplification with advanced-stage disease. Note this historical cohort reported 38% amplification, reflecting enrichment for advanced stage rather than the ~20% population figure.

genes/0.notes: MYCN amplification occurs in approximately 20% of neuroblastomas overall and is among the most powerful adverse genomic prognostic markers, used alongside stage, age, histology, 11q status, and ploidy for risk stratification. Reported frequencies vary substantially with cohort composition — historical series enriched for advanced-stage disease reported considerably higher rates.

evidence.snippet: The primary predisposition genes in familial neuroblastoma are ALK and PHOX2B.
evidence.explanation: Identifies ALK as a primary predisposition gene in familial neuroblastoma, consistent with its role as an oncogenic driver.

evidence.snippet: Our results demonstrate that heritable mutations of ALK are the main cause of familial neuroblastoma, and that germline or acquired activation of this cell-surface kinase is a tractable therapeutic target for this lethal paediatric malignancy.
evidence.explanation: The linkage-plus-resequencing study in neuroblastoma pedigrees that established ALK as the principal hereditary neuroblastoma gene, supporting the majority (not ~50%) framing of germline ALK in familial disease.

evidence.snippet: Resequencing in 194 high-risk neuroblastoma samples showed somatically acquired mutations in the tyrosine kinase domain in 12.4% of samples.
evidence.explanation: Quantifies somatic ALK tyrosine-kinase-domain mutation in a high-risk cohort at 12.4%; the 8-10% figure cited in the notes refers to unselected neuroblastoma, which is enriched for lower-risk disease.

genes/1.notes: ALK point mutations occur in 8-10% of sporadic neuroblastoma. Germline ALK mutations account for the large majority of hereditary neuroblastoma pedigrees — commonly reported at roughly 75-80% — making ALK the principal neuroblastoma predisposition gene. F1174L and R1275Q are the most common mutations. ALK is a therapeutic target for crizotinib and, in current frontline cooperative-group trials, lorlatinib.

evidence.snippet: Stage, age, histologic category, grade of tumor differentiation, the status of the MYCN oncogene, chromosome 11q status, and DNA ploidy were the most highly statistically significant and clinically relevant factors.
evidence.explanation: Establishes chromosome 11q status as a statistically significant, clinically relevant prognostic factor in a large patient cohort and as a formal component of INRG risk classification.

evidence.snippet: we identified key features of NB, including loss of NF1 and gain of 17q chromosome, which are critical for the development of malignant tumor.
evidence.explanation: Supports 17q gain specifically, and only as a feature acquired in an engineered iPSC-derived neural crest model transplanted into mice — not as patient-derived prognostic data. Marked PARTIAL because the cited work addresses neither 1p nor 11q deletion nor clinical outcome; the prognostic claim rests on the INRG evidence above.

genes/2.notes: Segmental chromosomal aberrations including 1p deletion, 11q deletion, and 17q gain are associated with worse prognosis and help define risk stratification. Chromosome 11q status is one of the factors formally incorporated into the INRG classification system; 11q deletion is characteristically found in MYCN-non-amplified high-risk disease.

evidence.snippet: These rearrangements occurred only in high-risk neuroblastomas (12/39, 31%) in a mutually exclusive fashion with MYCN amplifications and ATRX mutations, which are known genetic events in this tumour type.
evidence.explanation: Establishes TERT rearrangement as a high-risk-restricted event that is mutually exclusive with MYCN amplification and ATRX mutation, defining the three-way telomere-maintenance structure of neuroblastoma genomics.

evidence.snippet: TERT rearrangements defined a subgroup of high-risk tumours with particularly poor outcome.
evidence.explanation: Links TERT rearrangement to adverse outcome in an extended case series.

genes/3.notes: Genomic rearrangements juxtaposing enhancers to the TERT locus drive massive TERT upregulation and telomerase-mediated telomere maintenance. TERT rearrangement occurs in high-risk disease and is largely mutually exclusive with MYCN amplification and ATRX mutation, defining one of three alternative routes to telomere maintenance in neuroblastoma.

evidence.snippet: ATRX mutations were associated with an absence of the ATRX protein in the nucleus and with long telomeres.
evidence.explanation: Links ATRX mutation to loss of nuclear ATRX protein and to the long telomeres characteristic of alternative lengthening of telomeres.

evidence.snippet: ATRX mutations were associated with age at diagnosis in children and young adults with stage 4 neuroblastoma.
evidence.explanation: Whole-genome sequencing across 104 patients establishes the age dependence of ATRX mutation, supporting the adolescent/young-adult subtype framing.

genes/4.notes: Somatic ATRX loss-of-function drives telomere maintenance by the alternative lengthening of telomeres (ALT) pathway. ATRX-mutant neuroblastoma is strongly age-dependent, characterising an adolescent/young-adult subtype with indolent but chronically progressive, treatment-refractory disease. ATRX mutation is essentially absent in infants and is mutually exclusive with MYCN amplification.

evidence.snippet: The primary predisposition genes in familial neuroblastoma are ALK and PHOX2B.
evidence.explanation: Identifies PHOX2B alongside ALK as one of the two primary familial neuroblastoma predisposition genes.

genes/5.notes: PHOX2B is a master regulator of autonomic nervous system development and the second recognised hereditary neuroblastoma predisposition gene after ALK. Germline PHOX2B mutations cause neuroblastoma predisposition that may co-occur with other neurocristopathies — Hirschsprung disease and congenital central hypoventilation syndrome — reflecting a shared neural-crest developmental origin.

treatments/0.description: Chemotherapy intensity varies by risk group. Low-risk patients may need only observation or minimal chemotherapy. High-risk patients receive intensive induction chemotherapy including cisplatin, etoposide, vincristine, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, and topotecan.

treatments/1.description: Surgery for primary tumor resection is performed after chemotherapy for high-risk disease. Complete resection is associated with better outcomes when achievable without significant morbidity.

treatments/2.description: High-dose chemotherapy with autologous stem cell rescue is standard for high-risk neuroblastoma following induction chemotherapy and surgical resection. Tandem transplant may provide additional benefit.

treatments/3.description: Radiation to the primary tumor bed is used in high-risk disease following surgical resection and stem cell transplant.

treatments/4.description: Anti-GD2 monoclonal antibody (dinutuximab) combined with GM-CSF and IL-2 has significantly improved outcomes in high-risk neuroblastoma during maintenance therapy. GD2 is highly expressed on neuroblastoma cells.

treatments/5.description: ALK tyrosine kinase inhibition targets the constitutive ALK signalling produced by activating ALK point mutations or ALK amplification. The first-generation inhibitor crizotinib has limited activity against several common neuroblastoma ALK variants (notably F1174L), which motivated the move to third-generation, CNS-penetrant inhibitors; lorlatinib is under evaluation in frontline cooperative-group trials for ALK-altered high-risk disease. Applicable only to the ALK-altered molecular subset.

evidence.snippet: Mutations resulted in constitutive phosphorylation, and targeted knockdown of ALK messenger RNA resulted in profound inhibition of growth in all cell lines harbouring mutant or amplified ALK
evidence.explanation: Establishes ALK dependence of ALK-mutant and ALK-amplified neuroblastoma cells, the mechanistic rationale for ALK-directed therapy. Genetic knockdown rather than pharmacologic inhibition.

treatments/5/targets/0.description: ATP-competitive inhibition of the ALK tyrosine kinase domain abolishes the constitutive receptor autophosphorylation produced by activating ALK mutations, removing the downstream proliferative signal.

treatments/6.description: 13-cis-retinoic acid (isotretinoin) is given during maintenance therapy to promote differentiation of residual neuroblastoma cells and reduce relapse risk.

evidence.snippet: We found that she is compound heterozygous for mutations in the RAD50 gene that give rise to low levels of unstable RAD50 protein.
evidence.explanation: Directly establishes reduced, unstable RAD50 protein as the primary molecular lesion.

evidence.snippet: Immunoblotting experiments showed strongly reduced protein levels of RAD50 in the patient-derived fibroblasts
evidence.explanation: Independent confirmation of reduced RAD50 protein in patient cells.

evidence.snippet: Null mutants of each are inviable.
evidence.explanation: Supports the hypomorphic-allele requirement: complete loss of any MRN component is lethal in mouse, which is the basis for inferring that viable human patients retain partial RAD50 function. The lethality result is murine, not human.

steps/1.description: Biallelic hypomorphic RAD50 variants (nonsense, frameshift, splice-disrupting, stop-readthrough and in-frame deletion alleles) reduce the level or stability of RAD50, the SMC-family ATPase that bridges broken DNA ends within the MRN complex. Rad50-null mice are inviable and no human with complete RAD50 loss has been reported, so viable patients are inferred to retain partial function. Note that the lethality evidence is murine; the inference to human viability has not been tested directly.

evidence.snippet: failure to form DNA damage-induced MRN foci
evidence.explanation: Directly documents failure of MRN focus formation in RAD50-deficient patient cells.

evidence.snippet: The MRE11/RAD50/NBN (MRN) complex plays a key role in recognizing and signaling DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs).
evidence.explanation: Establishes the DSB-sensing role of the complex that RAD50 deficiency disrupts.

evidence.snippet: The expression of RAD50 protein and MRN complex formation was maintained in the cells derived from this patient.
evidence.explanation: Qualifies the node: in some RAD50 genotypes the complex still assembles, so the downstream signalling failure is not simply a consequence of absent complex.

evidence.snippet: MRN senses DSBs through a tight clamp-like sensing state with closed coiled-coil domains, but auto-inhibited MRE11 nuclease. NBS1 wraps around the MRE11 dimer, with NBS1's ATM recruitment motif sequestered by binding to the regulatory RAD50 S site, necessitating a switch in the NBS1 C helix for ATM activation.
evidence.explanation: Cryo-EM structures show that RAD50 directly gates ATM activation through its regulatory S site, giving a structural basis for why RAD50 lesions abolish ATM signalling even when the complex still assembles.

steps/2.description: The MRN complex is among the first entities recruited to a double-strand break. In RAD50-deficient patient cells, damage-induced MRN nuclear focus formation fails. The defect is in damage-recruited focus formation and sensing, NOT necessarily in complex assembly: the RAD50 E1035del coiled-coil allele still assembles an MRN complex but impairs MRE11 nuclease function and end resection, and in the p.Arg83His/p.Glu485Ter patient RAD50 expression and complex formation were maintained while ATM signalling still failed. Cryo-EM shows why assembly and signalling are separable - NBS1's ATM-recruitment motif is sequestered on the regulatory RAD50 S site and must be released for ATM activation, so RAD50 lesions can block signalling from within an intact complex.

evidence.snippet: impaired radiation-induced activation of and downstream signaling through the ATM protein, which is defective in the human genetic disorder ataxia-telangiectasia
evidence.explanation: Directly documents impaired ATM activation and downstream signalling in patient cells.

evidence.snippet: DNA damage-induced activation of the ATM kinase was markedly decreased, which was restored by the expression of wild-type (WT) RAD50.
evidence.explanation: Complementation with wild-type RAD50 rescues ATM activation, establishing that the signalling defect is directly caused by the RAD50 lesion.

evidence.snippet: provided evidence for a markedly reduced radiation-induced AT-mutated signaling
evidence.explanation: Independent confirmation of reduced radiation-induced ATM signalling.

steps/3.description: Radiation-induced activation of the ATM kinase and phosphorylation of its downstream substrates are markedly reduced in RAD50-deficient patient fibroblasts, phenocopying the signalling defect of ataxia-telangiectasia. Complementation with wild-type RAD50 restores ATM activation, establishing the dependency.

evidence.snippet: This mutation represents a human RAD50 separation-of-function mutation that impairs DNA repair, DNA replication, and DNA end resection without affecting ATM-dependent DNA damage response.
evidence.explanation: Establishes an ATM-independent resection/repair arm of RAD50 pathogenesis and its genetic separability from the checkpoint-signalling arm.

evidence.snippet: Purified recombinant proteins indicate that RAD50E1035Δ impairs MRE11 nuclease activity.
evidence.explanation: Biochemical demonstration that the RAD50 lesion acts by impairing MRE11 nuclease activity.

steps/4.description: RAD50 regulates MRE11-dependent 5'-3' end resection, the committed step of homology-directed repair, and also supports replication-fork function. The RAD50 E1035del coiled-coil allele demonstrates that this arm is genetically separable from ATM signalling, defining a separation-of-function mechanism within NBSLD.

evidence.snippet: These cells were also impaired in G1/S cell-cycle-checkpoint activation and displayed radioresistant DNA synthesis and G2-phase accumulation.
evidence.explanation: Directly documents checkpoint failure, RDS and G2 accumulation in patient cells.

evidence.snippet: Using patient-derived primary fibroblasts, we could show abnormal radioresistant DNA synthesis confirming pathogenicity of the identified variant.
evidence.explanation: Independent confirmation of radioresistant DNA synthesis in a second patient.

steps/5.description: Patient fibroblasts fail to activate the G1/S checkpoint, continue DNA synthesis after irradiation (radioresistant DNA synthesis, RDS) and accumulate in G2. RDS is the key functional diagnostic readout of NBSLD, shared with ataxia-telangiectasia, NBS and ATLD.

evidence.snippet: Cells from the patient were characterized by chromosomal instability; radiosensitivity
evidence.explanation: Directly documents chromosomal instability and radiosensitivity in RAD50-deficient cells.

evidence.snippet: The defective cellular phenotype was rescued by wild-type RAD50.
evidence.explanation: Complementation rescue establishes that the cellular instability phenotype is caused by the RAD50 lesion rather than by an unlinked variant.

steps/6.description: RAD50-deficient cells display spontaneous chromosomal instability and hypersensitivity to ionizing radiation. This is the cellular hallmark shared across the chromosomal instability syndromes and underlies the clinical recommendation to minimise radiation-based imaging.

evidence.snippet: The data indicate that even subtle perturbation of Mre11 complex functions results in severe genotoxic stress, and that the complex is critically important for homeostasis of proliferative tissues.
evidence.explanation: Establishes in a hypomorphic Rad50 mouse that partial MRN perturbation selectively compromises proliferative tissue homeostasis via genotoxic stress.

evidence.snippet: Rad50(S/S) mice died with complete bone marrow depletion as a result of progressive hematopoietic stem cell failure.
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates progressive haematopoietic stem cell attrition as the consequence of hypomorphic Rad50.

steps/7.description: Even subtle perturbation of MRN complex function generates severe genotoxic stress that is disproportionately borne by rapidly dividing progenitor compartments - neural progenitors during corticogenesis, somatic growth plates, and haematopoietic stem cells. This is the proposed convergence point linking a housekeeping DNA-repair defect to a selective growth, neurodevelopmental and marrow phenotype. The progenitor-attrition mechanism is directly demonstrated in Rad50(S/S) mice; its application to the human neurodevelopmental phenotype remains an inference.

evidence.snippet: These findings indicate important roles of RAD50 in human bone marrow and immune cells.
evidence.explanation: Establishes a RAD50-dependent requirement in human marrow and immune compartments.

evidence.snippet: Here, we identify a patient with bone marrow failure and developmental defects caused by biallelic RAD50 mutations.
evidence.explanation: Independent report linking biallelic RAD50 mutations to bone marrow failure.

steps/8.description: In an allele-dependent subset of patients, RAD50 deficiency decompensates the haematopoietic and B-lineage compartments, producing bone marrow failure and B-cell immunodeficiency - the feature that makes NBSLD, in these patients, an inborn error of immunity rather than a purely dysmorphic/growth syndrome.

evidence.snippet: Here, we report on a patient previously diagnosed as probably having NBS, with microcephaly, mental retardation, 'bird-like' face, and short stature.
evidence.explanation: Directly documents microcephaly in the index RAD50-deficient patient.

evidence.snippet: Human RAD50 gene mutations cause Nijmegen Breakage Syndrome-like disease, characterized by severe prenatal and postpartum growth retardation and microcephaly.
evidence.explanation: Characterises microcephaly as a defining feature of the disorder, supporting the VERY_FREQUENT band.

evidence.snippet: who presented with bilateral cryptorchidism, severe microcephaly, growth retardation, multiple café-au-lait macules, brachydactyly, and distinctive craniofacial features
evidence.explanation: Confirms severe microcephaly in an additional independently reported patient.

steps/9.description: Severe microcephaly, present congenitally, is a cardinal and near-invariant feature of NBSLD and one of the features that originally prompted a clinical diagnosis of Nijmegen breakage syndrome in the index patient.

evidence.snippet: characterized by severe prenatal and postpartum growth retardation and microcephaly
evidence.explanation: Directly documents prenatal (intrauterine) growth retardation as a defining feature.

steps/10.description: Growth restriction in NBSLD begins prenatally, distinguishing it from postnatal-onset growth failure syndromes.

evidence.snippet: The boy was born at full term, with substantial growth retardation from infancy to early childhood.
evidence.explanation: Documents postnatal growth retardation from infancy in a reported NBSLD patient.

steps/11.description: Growth restriction continues after birth; in one reported patient height was -3.35 SD before growth hormone therapy.

evidence.snippet: with microcephaly, mental retardation, 'bird-like' face, and short stature
evidence.explanation: Documents short stature in the index patient.

evidence.snippet: we report a long-term follow-up of an unrelated patient with facial dysmorphisms, microcephaly, skeletal features, and short stature
evidence.explanation: Confirms short stature in the second reported patient.

evidence.snippet: We report on a girl with microcephaly, mental retardation, bird-like face, short stature, bone marrow failure and B-cell immunodeficiency.
evidence.explanation: Confirms short stature in a third independently reported patient.

Preferred over a 3/3 count derived from individual case reports because it is an explicit multi-patient statement. Snippet retains the source PDF's line breaks and ligature/spacing artifacts so it matches the cached body exactly.

steps/12.description: Short stature is reported in essentially every molecularly confirmed NBSLD patient and is frequently the presenting complaint that triggers endocrine referral.

evidence.snippet: Mild intellectual impairment was confirmed on formal neurocognitive testing.
evidence.explanation: Formal neurocognitive testing documenting mild intellectual impairment.

evidence.snippet: with microcephaly, mental retardation, 'bird-like' face, and short stature
evidence.explanation: Documents intellectual disability in the index patient; the abstract does not grade severity, so this supports the phenotype but not specifically the "mild" qualifier.

This resolves the earlier gap where no source graded severity across patients. Snippet retains the source PDF line breaks so it matches the cached body exactly.

steps/13.description: Cognitive impairment in NBSLD is generally mild and, in the best-followed patients, non-progressive - a contrast with the progressive neurodegeneration of ataxia-telangiectasia-like disorder.

evidence.snippet: with microcephaly, mental retardation, 'bird-like' face, and short stature
evidence.explanation: Directly documents bird-like facies in the index patient.

evidence.snippet: We report on a girl with microcephaly, mental retardation, bird-like face, short stature, bone marrow failure and B-cell immunodeficiency.
evidence.explanation: Confirms bird-like facies in an independently reported patient.

steps/14.description: A "bird-like" facial gestalt is a recurrent recognisable feature shared with Nijmegen breakage syndrome and is often what prompts genetic evaluation. In the individually described patients the craniofacial profile comprised a sloping forehead, midface prominence and a receding mandible; those are per-patient observations rather than a definition of the bird-like gestalt, and are curated separately as Sloping forehead and Retrognathia.

evidence.snippet: including a sloping forehead, midface prominence, and receding mandible
evidence.explanation: Directly documents a sloping forehead as part of the craniofacial phenotype.

steps/15.description: A sloping forehead, together with midface prominence and a receding mandible, forms the distinctive craniofacial profile of NBSLD.

evidence.snippet: severe microcephaly, growth retardation, multiple café-au-lait macules, brachydactyly
evidence.explanation: Directly documents multiple cafe-au-lait macules in a reported NBSLD patient.

steps/16.description: Multiple cafe-au-lait macules have been reported in NBSLD, a pigmentary feature that also occurs in other chromosomal instability syndromes and can prompt consideration of constitutional mismatch repair deficiency or neurofibromatosis type 1.

evidence.snippet: multiple café-au-lait macules, brachydactyly, and distinctive craniofacial features
evidence.explanation: Directly documents brachydactyly in a reported NBSLD patient.

steps/17.description: Digital shortening is part of the reported skeletal phenotype of NBSLD.

evidence.snippet: We report a 6-year-old Chinese boy, who presented with bilateral cryptorchidism, severe microcephaly, growth retardation
evidence.explanation: Directly documents bilateral cryptorchidism in a reported NBSLD patient.

steps/18.description: Bilateral cryptorchidism was reported in a male NBSLD patient, expanding the recognised phenotypic spectrum.

evidence.snippet: Cells from the patient were characterized by chromosomal instability; radiosensitivity
evidence.explanation: Directly documents chromosomal instability in RAD50-deficient patient cells.

evidence.snippet: Nijmegen breakage syndrome-like disorder (NBSLD) is a rare chromosomal instability syndrome caused by biallelic pathogenic variants in RAD50
evidence.explanation: Classifies NBSLD as a chromosomal instability syndrome.

steps/19.description: Spontaneous chromosomal instability in patient cells is a defining cytogenetic laboratory feature and the basis of the "chromosomal instability syndrome" classification. As with radiosensitivity, the cytogenetic finding is genotype-dependent and not uniformly present - a normal karyotype has been reported alongside abnormal radioresistant DNA synthesis - so a normal breakage study does not exclude the diagnosis.

evidence.snippet: Cells from the patient were characterized by chromosomal instability; radiosensitivity
evidence.explanation: Directly documents cellular radiosensitivity in the index patient.

evidence.snippet: Radiosensitivity appeared inconspicuous in the patient-derived cell line as assessed by colony formation assay.
evidence.explanation: Qualifies the phenotype: radiosensitivity is genotype-dependent and was not detectable by colony formation assay in this patient, so a normal assay does not exclude NBSLD.

steps/20.description: Cellular radiosensitivity reflects defective double-strand break repair and is the basis for the clinical recommendation to prefer MRI/ultrasound over CT and plain radiography. Radiosensitivity is not uniform across genotypes - in one patient with preserved MRN complex formation it was inconspicuous by colony formation assay.

evidence.snippet: RAD50 deficiency/NBSLD can manifest as a distinct inborn error of immunity characterized by bone marrow failure and B-cell immunodeficiency.
evidence.explanation: Directly documents bone marrow failure as part of the NBSLD spectrum.

evidence.snippet: Here, we identify a patient with bone marrow failure and developmental defects caused by biallelic RAD50 mutations.
evidence.explanation: Independent report of bone marrow failure in a biallelic RAD50 patient.

steps/21.description: Bone marrow failure occurs in an allele-dependent subset of NBSLD patients and is the principal determinant of prognosis in that group.

evidence.snippet: We report on a girl with microcephaly, mental retardation, bird-like face, short stature, bone marrow failure and B-cell immunodeficiency.
evidence.explanation: Directly documents B-cell immunodeficiency in a RAD50-deficient patient.

steps/22.description: B-cell immunodeficiency accompanies bone marrow failure in the severe arm of the RAD50-deficiency spectrum.

evidence.snippet: RAD50 deficiency/NBSLD can manifest as a distinct inborn error of immunity characterized by bone marrow failure and B-cell immunodeficiency.
evidence.explanation: Supports immunodeficiency specifically in the marrow-failure arm, establishing that the feature is allele-dependent rather than a disease-wide manifestation.

steps/23.description: Immunodeficiency is confined to the bone-marrow-failure arm of the RAD50 spectrum, where it takes the form of B-cell deficiency. It is deliberately scoped to that subtype rather than asserted for the disease as a whole, because its ABSENCE is the defining feature of classic NBSLD and of the MONDO/Orphanet disease definition.

evidence.snippet: The immunological assessment revealed borderline lymphopenia without overt immunodeficiency.
evidence.explanation: Documents borderline lymphopenia while explicitly excluding overt immunodeficiency in the same patient.

steps/24.description: Borderline lymphopenia without overt immunodeficiency has been reported in a classic NBSLD patient, indicating that mild immunological abnormalities can occur even in the arm that lacks clinical immunodeficiency.

evidence.snippet: P1 also developed a cataract at 10 years of age that necessitated surgical intervention.
evidence.explanation: Directly documents early-onset cataract requiring surgery in a RAD50-deficient patient.

steps/25.description: Early-onset cataract requiring surgery was documented at age 10 in the RAD50 E1035del patient, as part of a clinical picture the authors read as a DNA repair and/or telomere maintenance defect.

evidence.explanation: Quantified thrombocytopenia in the marrow-failure patient.

steps/26.description: Thrombocytopenia is part of the multilineage cytopenia of the marrow-failure arm.

evidence.snippet: P1's cell blood count revealed thrombocytopenia (platelet count of 113 G/L) associated with anemia (hemoglobin level of 10 g/dL) and neutropenia (neutrophil count of 1 G/L)
evidence.explanation: Quantified anemia in the marrow-failure patient.

steps/27.description: Anemia accompanies thrombocytopenia and neutropenia in the marrow-failure arm.

evidence.snippet: P1's cell blood count revealed thrombocytopenia (platelet count of 113 G/L) associated with anemia (hemoglobin level of 10 g/dL) and neutropenia (neutrophil count of 1 G/L)
evidence.explanation: Quantified neutropenia in the marrow-failure patient.

steps/28.description: Neutropenia completes the trilineage cytopenia of the marrow-failure arm.

evidence.snippet: Bone marrow smears and biopsies showed reduced cellularity (15%) without myelodysplastic features, consistent with aplastic anemia.
evidence.explanation: Documents quantified marrow hypocellularity read as aplastic anemia, explicitly excluding myelodysplasia.

steps/29.description: Marrow biopsy in the E1035del patient showed 15% cellularity without myelodysplastic features, which the authors read as aplastic anemia rather than a myelodysplastic process - a distinction that matters for management.

evidence.snippet: physical examination of P1 revealed failure to thrive (height of 108.5 cm, <3rd percentile; weight of 17.2 kg, <3rd percentile), skin pigmentation, nail dysplasia, leukoplakia, dental loss, microcephaly
evidence.explanation: Documents abnormal skin pigmentation as part of the mucocutaneous triad.

steps/30.description: Part of a dyskeratosis-congenita-like mucocutaneous triad (skin pigmentation, nail dysplasia, leukoplakia) reported in the marrow-failure patient. The triad is what drives the dyskeratosis congenita differential in this arm.

evidence.snippet: skin pigmentation, nail dysplasia, leukoplakia, dental loss, microcephaly
evidence.explanation: Documents nail dysplasia in the marrow-failure patient.

steps/31.description: Second component of the dyskeratosis-congenita-like mucocutaneous triad.

evidence.snippet: skin pigmentation, nail dysplasia, leukoplakia, dental loss, microcephaly
evidence.explanation: Documents leukoplakia in the marrow-failure patient.

steps/32.description: Third component of the dyskeratosis-congenita-like mucocutaneous triad.

evidence.snippet: skin pigmentation, nail dysplasia, leukoplakia, dental loss, microcephaly
evidence.explanation: Documents dental loss in the marrow-failure patient.

steps/33.description: Dental loss accompanied the mucocutaneous triad in the marrow-failure patient.

evidence.snippet: physical examination of P1 revealed failure to thrive (height of 108.5 cm, <3rd percentile; weight of 17.2 kg, <3rd percentile)
evidence.explanation: Documents quantified failure to thrive in a RAD50-deficient patient.

steps/34.description: Failure to thrive with height and weight below the 3rd percentile was documented in the marrow-failure patient, consistent with the growth restriction seen across the spectrum.

evidence.snippet: he had obvious facial deformities, including receding forehead, long and narrow nasal bridge, small and prominent mouth, smooth and short philtrum, and micrognathia
evidence.explanation: Directly documents micrognathia within the craniofacial phenotype.

steps/35.description: Micrognathia is independently reported alongside the receding-mandible description, forming part of the recurrent craniofacial profile.

evidence.snippet: including a sloping forehead, midface prominence, and receding mandible
evidence.explanation: Directly documents a receding mandible as part of the craniofacial phenotype.

steps/36.description: A receding mandible is part of the reported craniofacial profile of NBSLD.

edges/1.description: Loss of the RAD50 ATPase scaffold prevents productive assembly and recruitment of the MRE11-RAD50-NBN complex at double-strand breaks.

edges/2.description:
The first of eight extra-haematopoietic malformations drawn from the germline lesion itself rather than from any downstream step, and the reason is worth stating once here for all of them. The genotoxic-stress node below scopes itself to a growth, neurodevelopmental and marrow phenotype, and its evidence covers proliferative-tissue homeostasis; limb, ocular, genital, pigmentary and ectodermal development are outside that scope. No cited source traces a route from RAD50 loss to any of them, so they attach where the only established fact places them — at the germline lesion — which is also how the sibling ERCC6L2 and SRP72 entries handle their equivalently unexplained non-haematologic features.
Brachydactyly itself is limb-bud derived and is reported together with the microcephaly and growth retardation in the same patients.

edges/3.description: The ocular malformation. The lens epithelium is a renewing tissue, so a replication-stress account is available, but it is not demonstrated and the node that would carry that account does not claim ocular scope.

edges/4.description: Reported among the developmental findings. Germ cells are among the most replication-dependent lineages, which makes a replication-stress account more plausible here than for the other malformations in this group — still untraced, and still not within the scope the genotoxic-stress node claims.

edges/5.description: Pigmentary lesions reported with the microcephaly, growth retardation and brachydactyly in the same series.

edges/6.description: The broader pigmentary abnormality, reported in the coiled-coil RAD50 patient alongside the three ectodermal findings below.

edges/7.description: One of three ectodermal features — with oral leukoplakia and premature dental loss — that give this RAD50 patient a presentation overlapping dyskeratosis congenita. That overlap is real and reported, not a curation error, but it is a single coiled-coil-variant report rather than a general feature of RAD50 disease.

edges/8.description: The mucosal member of that ectodermal triad. See the nail dysplasia edge for the scope caveat.

edges/9.description: The dental member of that ectodermal triad, reported in the same patient.

edges/10.description: MRN is required to recruit and activate ATM at breaks; its failure blunts the ATM-dependent phosphorylation cascade.

edges/11.description: RAD50 gates MRE11 nuclease access, so RAD50 defects impair initiation of resection and homology-directed repair.

edges/12.description: Loss of ATM-dependent signalling disables the G1/S and intra-S checkpoints that normally suppress DNA synthesis after irradiation.

edges/13.description: Failure of homology-directed repair leaves double-strand breaks to be resolved by error-prone routes, generating breaks and rearrangements.

edges/14.description: Replicating through unrepaired damage without checkpoint arrest converts lesions into chromosomal breaks and rearrangements.

edges/15.description: Persistent genome instability is most consequential in tissues with high proliferative demand.

edges/16.description: Defective double-strand break repair renders patient cells radiosensitive.

edges/17.description: Unrepaired double-strand breaks manifest cytogenetically as chromosome breakage.

evidence.snippet: The data indicate that even subtle perturbation of Mre11 complex functions results in severe genotoxic stress, and that the complex is critically important for homeostasis of proliferative tissues.
evidence.explanation: Supports the general proliferative-tissue-homeostasis premise in mouse. It does NOT demonstrate the neural-progenitor route to microcephaly, which is why this edge is typed INDIRECT_UNKNOWN_INTERMEDIATES and the evidence is INDIRECT.

edges/18.description: Depletion of the neural progenitor pool during corticogenesis is the inferred route to congenital microcephaly; the intermediate steps have not been demonstrated in human RAD50-deficient tissue.

evidence.snippet: We demonstrate here that hypomorphic Rad50 mutant mice (Rad50(S/S) mice) exhibited growth defects and cancer predisposition.
evidence.explanation: Hypomorphic Rad50 produces growth defects in mouse, supporting the growth arm of the mechanism; the prenatal timing in humans is not established by this result.

edges/19.description: Reduced proliferative capacity across somatic tissues restricts prenatal growth.

evidence.snippet: We demonstrate here that hypomorphic Rad50 mutant mice (Rad50(S/S) mice) exhibited growth defects and cancer predisposition.
evidence.explanation: Supports growth restriction as a consequence of hypomorphic Rad50 in mouse; the human postnatal course is documented clinically on the phenotype record itself.

edges/20.description: Continued restriction of proliferative growth produces postnatal short stature.

edges/21.description: The same neural-progenitor attrition inferred to cause microcephaly is the presumed route to the accompanying mild, non-progressive cognitive impairment.

edges/22.description: In the marrow-failure arm, haematopoietic stem and B-lineage progenitors are the compartment that decompensates.

edges/23.description: Growth failure continuing after birth, alongside the intrauterine growth retardation and short stature already drawn from this node.

edges/24.description: The clinical presentation of that growth failure in infancy.

edges/25.description: The characteristic craniofacial gestalt, of which the micrognathia, retrognathia and sloping forehead below are the components. All four are drawn from this node on one basis and it is worth being explicit about how weak it is: proliferating progenitor pools include the neural crest and cranial mesenchyme, so a replication-stress mechanism is plausible, but no cited source traces a route from RAD50 loss to any individual craniofacial feature. The link type records that.

edges/26.description: A component of the craniofacial gestalt above.

edges/27.description: A component of the craniofacial gestalt above.

edges/28.description: A component of the craniofacial gestalt, and the one most closely tied to the microcephaly already drawn from this node.

edges/29.description: Haematopoietic stem cell failure manifests as marrow hypocellularity.

edges/30.description: The B-lineage compartment is selectively depleted.

edges/31.description: The clinical diagnosis the marrow failure arrives at. Curated alongside the individual cytopenias below because sources describe both the syndrome and its components.

edges/32.description: The erythroid consequence of failing marrow output.

edges/33.description: The megakaryocytic consequence of failing marrow output.

edges/34.description: The granulocytic consequence of failing marrow output.

edges/35.description: Total lymphopenia, of which the selectively depleted B compartment above is the dominant but not the only component.

edges/36.description: The functional consequence of the B-lineage and lymphocyte depletion. This is the feature that places the disease in the IUIS classification at all, so it is curated as its own phenotype rather than left implicit in the cell counts.

evidence.snippet: In conclusion, we have identified and characterized a patient with a RAD50 deficiency that results in a clinical phenotype that can be classified as an NBS-like disorder (NBSLD).
evidence.explanation: Establishes RAD50 as the causal gene for NBSLD.

evidence.snippet: caused by biallelic pathogenic variants in RAD50, which is a key component of the MRE11-RAD50-NBS1 (MRN) complex involved in DNA double-strand break repair
evidence.explanation: Confirms biallelic RAD50 variants as the molecular cause and situates RAD50 in the MRN complex.

evidence.snippet: To date, no disease due to RAD50 deficiency has been described.
evidence.explanation: Records that this report established the gene-disease relationship for RAD50, which had no prior disease association.

genes/0.notes: Reported alleles span nonsense, frameshift, splice-disrupting, stop-codon-readthrough and in-frame single-residue deletion classes. Monoallelic RAD50 variants are a separate question (cancer susceptibility) and do not cause NBSLD.

evidence.snippet: Although recombinant human growth hormone significantly improved the patient's growth rate (from -3.35 SD to -1.28 SD), these variants may serve as a potential molecular basis for Nijmegen Breakage Syndrome-like disease and could also increase the risk of tumor formation.
evidence.explanation: Reports both the growth benefit and the explicit tumour-risk caution attached to it in the single documented NBSLD growth hormone experience.

evidence.snippet: At the age of 4.5 years, the child with syndromic short stature was prescribed recombinant human growth hormone for height correction by junior resident physicians, with no genetic evaluation performed prior to treatment.
evidence.explanation: Documents the safety lesson that the therapy was given without prior genetic evaluation, which the report frames as the central cautionary finding.

treatments/0.description: Somatropin has been used off-label for the short stature of NBSLD. In the single reported experience, 5 years 9 months of therapy improved height from -3.35 SD to -1.28 SD with no tumour at 5-year post-discontinuation follow-up. IMPORTANT SAFETY CAVEAT - in that case growth hormone was started by junior physicians before any genetic evaluation; the authors emphasise that genetic evaluation should precede growth-promoting therapy in syndromic short stature, because growth hormone/IGF-1 signalling is mitogenic and the underlying DNA repair deficiency may raise tumour risk. The evidence base is one patient.

evidence.snippet: However, it is not presently required for this patient, who is managed with regular surveillance.
evidence.explanation: Documents surveillance-based management as the current standard for an NBSLD patient.

evidence.snippet: Due to the DNA damage repair defect, repeated X-ray or CT scans should be avoided, and MRI or ultrasound scans should be used instead.
evidence.explanation: Directly supports the imaging-modality recommendation, which was previously asserted in the description without a supporting citation.

treatments/1.description: In the absence of any disease-modifying therapy, reported NBSLD patients are managed with regular clinical surveillance and multidisciplinary supportive care. Because patient cells are radiosensitive, non-ionizing imaging (MRI, ultrasound) is preferred over CT and plain radiography where feasible.

evidence.snippet: Allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) has been proposed as a potential therapeutic option for DNA damage repair disorders.
evidence.explanation: Supports HSCT as a proposed option for DNA damage repair disorders; the same report makes clear it was not required in this patient, so the evidence is partial.

treatments/2.description: HSCT has been proposed as a potential therapeutic option for DNA damage repair disorders and would be the standard consideration for the bone-marrow-failure arm of NBSLD. It has been raised but not required in the reported cases, so this is a proposed rather than established indication for this specific disorder.

treatments/2/targets/0.description: Replacing the RAD50-deficient haematopoietic stem cell compartment with donor cells removes the failing compartment itself. It does not correct the RAD50 defect in neural, skeletal or other somatic tissue, so it addresses only the haematologic arm.

treatments/3.description: Autosomal recessive inheritance carries a 25% recurrence risk per pregnancy for carrier couples. Counseling should also cover the recommendation that molecular diagnosis precede any elective growth-promoting therapy.

evidence.snippet: This mutation represents a human RAD50 separation-of-function mutation that impairs DNA repair, DNA replication, and DNA end resection without affecting ATM-dependent DNA damage response.
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates that RAD50 alleles can dissociate MRN sub-functions, the premise of the hypothesis.

evidence.snippet: Eight missense variants, all capable of forming an MRN complex, supported the DNA damage response and mitotic features to different extents, indicating these functions are separable.
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates that RAD50 variants separate the damage-response and mitotic functions. Note the variants tested were cancer-related RAD50 missense alleles, not NBSLD patient alleles, so this supports the general principle of functional separability rather than the specific classic-versus-marrow-failure split.

evidence.snippet: Functional heterogeneity of RAD50 variants could contribute to clinical variability.
evidence.explanation: Systematic functional dissection of cancer-related RAD50 missense variants explicitly proposes allele-level functional heterogeneity as a source of clinical variability - the premise this hypothesis extends to the NBSLD allelic spectrum, which the study itself did not test.

hypotheses/0.description: Reported RAD50 genotypes segregate into a "classic" arm with growth failure and microcephaly but preserved immunity, and an arm with bone marrow failure and B-cell immunodeficiency. The proposed explanation is that different alleles preserve different MRN sub-functions: the E1035del coiled-coil allele impairs end resection and replication while sparing ATM signalling, whereas the p.Arg83His/p.Glu485Ter genotype preserves complex assembly but abolishes ATM activation. Which sub-function is retained is hypothesised to determine whether the haematopoietic/B-cell compartment decompensates. This mapping is inferred from a handful of patients and has not been tested systematically.

evidence.snippet: these variants may serve as a potential molecular basis for Nijmegen Breakage Syndrome-like disease and could also increase the risk of tumor formation
evidence.explanation: Authors of the only treated case explicitly raise unresolved tumour risk despite the absence of observed malignancy.

evidence.snippet:
due to the rarity of cases and the short follow-up period, we cannot
rule out the possibility that patients with NBSLD caused by RAD50
mutations are at an increased risk of malignancy. Patients with
NBSLD caused by RAD50 mutations should be regularly monitored
for tumor occurrence.
evidence.explanation: States the knowledge gap directly in the authors' own words - rarity and short follow-up prevent excluding increased malignancy risk - and gives the resulting surveillance recommendation. This is the primary warrant for this discussion.

evidence.snippet: hypomorphic Rad50 mutant mice (Rad50(S/S) mice) exhibited growth defects and cancer predisposition
evidence.explanation: The hypomorphic mouse model does show cancer predisposition, which is what makes the human observation surprising and the gap worth resolving.

open_questions/0.rationale: No malignancy has been reported in the longest-followed NBSLD patients (index patient malignancy-free at 23 years; a growth-hormone-treated patient tumour-free at 5-year follow-up). But the total published cohort is fewer than ten patients with variable follow-up, and both the paralogous human diseases (NBS, ATLD) and the hypomorphic Rad50(S/S) mouse show clear cancer predisposition. Absence of evidence here is not evidence of absence, and case-report authors explicitly flag increased tumour risk when considering mitogenic therapy.

evidence.snippet: whereas CHEK2 c.1100delC, MCPH1 c.909_921del, and RAD50 c.687delT were moderate-risk alleles
evidence.explanation: Establishes moderate breast-cancer risk specifically for the recurrent RAD50 c.687delT allele in a Northern Finnish population-based case-control study; it does not generalise to all heterozygous RAD50 variants or to any population.

open_questions/1.rationale: This is a carrier-level question, deliberately kept out of the disease's genetic record because it is not evidence about NBSLD itself. Monoallelic RAD50 loss-of-function is studied as a breast-cancer susceptibility allele, but the risk is not uniform across alleles: a Northern Finnish population-based study classified the recurrent founder allele RAD50 c.687delT as a moderate-risk allele, whereas broader analyses of heterozygous RAD50 pathogenic variants have not shown a consistent overall breast-cancer excess. Cascade testing after an NBSLD diagnosis will identify obligate carrier parents, so the scope and limits of that risk statement matter practically. Nothing here implies a cancer risk statement for the biallelic disease.

evidence.snippet: Rad50(S/S) mice died with complete bone marrow depletion as a result of progressive hematopoietic stem cell failure.
evidence.explanation: The mouse's lethal marrow phenotype is the specific outcome that does not match classic human NBSLD.

evidence.snippet: she never had severe infections, had normal immunoglobulin levels, and did not develop lymphoid malignancy up to age 23 years
evidence.explanation: The human classic phenotype lacks the haematologic and oncologic outcomes that dominate the mouse model.

open_questions/2.rationale: The progenitor-attrition mechanism invoked for human growth failure and microcephaly is demonstrated principally in Rad50(S/S) mice, but that model's dominant outcomes - lethal haematopoietic failure and tumours - correspond to the minority bone-marrow-failure arm of the human spectrum, not the classic arm. Conversely, no mouse model reproduces the severe congenital microcephaly that defines human NBSLD. Because Rad50 nulls are embryonically lethal, viable models necessarily carry particular hypomorphic alleles whose residual activity may not correspond to any human genotype, so mechanistic inferences drawn from the mouse for the human neurodevelopmental phenotype have uncertain translational validity.

evidence.snippet: The E50K mutant strongly interacted with TANK-binding kinase 1 (TBK1), which prohibited the proper oligomerization and solubility of OPTN, both of which are important for OPTN intracellular transition.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the enhanced E50K-TBK1 interaction and the resulting loss of proper oligomerization and solubility that define this node.

evidence.snippet: Over-expression of E50K in HEK293 cells indicated accumulation of insoluble OPTN in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER).
evidence.explanation: Localizes the insoluble mutant protein to the endoplasmic reticulum.

evidence.snippet: In cells expressing OPTN bearing the most common glaucoma-associated mutation, E50K, covalent oligomers were formed even without H2O2 stimulation.
evidence.explanation: Shows that E50K alone drives the covalent cross-linked oligomer state that wild-type optineurin adopts only under oxidative stress, supporting the misfolding characterization of this node.

steps/2.description: A heterozygous missense change in OPTN - most commonly p.Glu50Lys (E50K), the recurrent allele in normal-tension glaucoma pedigrees - alters the biophysical behaviour of optineurin. Mutant OPTN binds TANK-binding kinase 1 (TBK1) abnormally strongly, which blocks the normal oligomerization and solubility that optineurin needs for its intracellular transitions, and the insoluble protein accumulates in the endoplasmic reticulum. Independently, E50K drives formation of covalently cross-linked optineurin oligomers of the kind normally seen only under oxidative stress. This is a toxic gain-of-function lesion rather than simple haploinsufficiency, which is why heterozygosity suffices and why TBK1 is a tractable drug target one step downstream.

evidence.snippet: Optineurin was identified as an autophagy receptor that directly interacts with autophagosomal protein, LC3, and ubiquitin.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the normal autophagy-receptor role of optineurin that this node describes being lost. Evidence source is OTHER because this is a review.

evidence.snippet: Optineurin interacts with a motor protein, myosinVI, and this interaction is involved in mediating fusion of autophagosomes with lysosomes.
evidence.explanation: Supports the autophagosome-lysosome fusion step annotated on this node as an optineurin-dependent function. Evidence source is OTHER because this is a review.

evidence.snippet: Increased p62/SQSTM1 and LC3-II levels indicated that autophagic flux was inhibited and contributed to TDP-43 aggregation in vivo and in vitro.
evidence.explanation: Provides the direct flux measurement (LC3-II and p62 both up) behind the DECREASED macroautophagy annotation, in an E50K knock-in mouse and in E50K-expressing retinal cells.

evidence.snippet: We identified an impairment of autophagic-lysosomal degradation and decreased mTORC1 signaling via activation of the stress sensor AMPK, along with subsequent neurodegeneration in OPTN(E50K) RGCs differentiated from hPSCs
evidence.explanation: Human isogenic stem-cell-derived retinal ganglion cell evidence for both the autophagic-lysosomal block and the reduced mTORC1 signalling annotated on this node.

evidence.snippet: Mutations in OPTN and TBK1 cause a dysregulation of autophagy which may directly cause retinal ganglion cell damage and normal tension glaucoma.
evidence.explanation: States the autophagy-to-RGC-damage causal chain at the level of the human disease, complementing the cellular and mouse evidence above.

steps/3.description: Optineurin is a selective autophagy receptor: it binds polyubiquitinated cargo through its ubiquitin-binding domain and delivers it to nascent autophagosomes through its LC3-interacting region, and it links autophagosomes to lysosomes via myosin VI. Retinal ganglion cells express optineurin highly and, as long-lived post-mitotic neurons with an exceptional axonal maintenance burden, depend heavily on autophagic quality control. Mutant optineurin blocks flux through this pathway. In OPTN(E50K) mice and in E50K-expressing retinal cells, LC3-II and p62/SQSTM1 both accumulate - the signature of a downstream block rather than reduced initiation - and undegraded substrates including TDP-43 aggregate in the cytoplasm. In isogenic OPTN(E50K) human stem cell-derived retinal ganglion cells the same lesion is accompanied by AMPK activation and reduced mTORC1 signalling, and mTOR-independent induction of autophagy restores neurite outgrowth, showing the block is the proximate cause of the neurodegenerative phenotype rather than a bystander. This node conforms to the `disabled_macroautophagy` module's central effector: the failure point here is selective cargo recognition by the receptor itself, not the core ATG machinery, and it is genetic rather than age-associated, but the resulting loss of cytoplasmic quality control is the conserved state that module models.

evidence.snippet: Here, we uncover an unconventional path of PINK1/Parkin mitophagy initiation by OPTN that does not begin with FIP200 binding or require the ULK1/2 kinases.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the distinct, TBK1-dependent route by which optineurin initiates mitophagy, which is the mechanistic basis for treating this as a separate node from bulk autophagy.

evidence.snippet: Using gene-edited cell lines and in vitro reconstitutions, we show that OPTN utilizes the kinase TBK1, which binds directly to the class III phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase complex I to initiate mitophagy.
evidence.explanation: Names TBK1 as the initiating kinase for OPTN-driven mitophagy, linking this node back to the E50K-TBK1 lesion in the trigger node.

evidence.snippet: It is involved in xenophagy, mitophagy, aggrephagy, and tumor suppression.
evidence.explanation: Review confirming mitophagy as one of the selective-autophagy functions of optineurin. Evidence source is OTHER because this is a review.

steps/4.description: Optineurin is one of the principal mitophagy receptors of the PINK1/Parkin pathway, and it initiates mitophagy by an unconventional route: rather than recruiting FIP200 and the ULK1/2 complex as NDP52, TAX1BP1 and p62 do, OPTN uses TBK1 bound directly to the class III PI3K complex I. Because that initiation step runs through the very kinase whose interaction E50K perturbs, the mitophagy arm is not simply a special case of the general autophagy block but a mechanistically distinct point of vulnerability. Failure to clear damaged mitochondria leaves retinal ganglion cells - among the most energetically demanding neurons in the body, with long unmyelinated intraretinal axons - carrying a dysfunctional mitochondrial pool. This node is curated as an amplifier of, not a substitute for, the autophagic-flux lesion.

evidence.snippet: At the molecular level, introduction of the E50K mutation disrupts the interaction between Optn and Rab8 GTPase, a protein involved in the regulation of vesicle transport from Golgi to plasma membrane.
evidence.explanation: Directly demonstrates loss of the Optn-Rab8 interaction as a consequence of E50K, in the transgenic mouse study that first reported it.

evidence.snippet: Glaucoma-associated mutants of OPTN, E50K, and M98K, cause defective vesicle trafficking, autophagy, and signaling that contribute to death of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs).
evidence.explanation: Review placing defective vesicle trafficking alongside autophagy as a contributor to retinal ganglion cell death. Evidence source is OTHER because this is a review article.

steps/5.description: Beyond autophagy, optineurin acts as an effector and adaptor for the Rab8 GTPase, coupling Rab8 to myosin VI and to its GTPase-activating protein TBC1D17 to control Golgi-to-plasma-membrane vesicle transport and transferrin receptor recycling. The E50K substitution disrupts the Optn-Rab8 interaction. This trafficking arm is curated as a modifier rather than a second central effector: it is well demonstrated biochemically and in transgenic mouse retina, but the pathway from disturbed vesicle transport to ganglion cell death is less directly evidenced than the autophagic route.

evidence.snippet: A glaucoma-associated mutant of optineurin, E50K, impairs autophagy as well as vesicle trafficking, leading to death of retinal cells by apoptosis.
evidence.explanation: Connects the upstream autophagy and trafficking lesions to apoptotic retinal cell death. Evidence source is OTHER because this is a review. The quote says "retinal cells", not retinal ganglion cells: much of the cell work this review summarises was done in RGC-5 and 661W lines, and PMID:33723228 (cited elsewhere in this entry) reports RGC-5 not to be of RGC origin. It should therefore not be read as RGC-specific evidence - the ganglion-cell specificity of this node rests on the NeuN-labelled knock-in mouse retina (PMID:33723228) and the human iPSC-derived RGCs (PMID:39425218).

evidence.snippet: Loss of RGCs decreased retinal thickness and visual impairment were observed in OPTN (E50K) mice compared with WT mice.
evidence.explanation: In vivo ganglion cell loss in an E50K knock-in mouse, the animal counterpart of this node.

evidence.snippet: Moreover, overexpression of E50K OPTN induced R28 cell apoptosis.
evidence.explanation: Cell-based confirmation that mutant optineurin is sufficient to induce apoptosis in a retinal precursor line.

evidence.snippet: Transgenic mice expressing E50K-OPTN show loss of RGCs and persistent reactive gliosis.
evidence.explanation: Review corroborating ganglion cell loss with reactive gliosis in E50K transgenic mice. Evidence source is OTHER because this is a review.

steps/6.description: Retinal ganglion cells carrying mutant optineurin die by apoptosis. This is the node at which OPTN-related disease rejoins the conserved glaucomatous neurodegeneration captured by the `glaucoma_optic_neuropathy` module - but it is reached from a cell-autonomous proteostatic lesion rather than from the module's trabecular-outflow and elevated-IOP arm, which does not apply to this entity. E50K knock-in mice show reduced numbers of viable ganglion cells and raised cleaved caspase-3 in the retina at intraocular pressures indistinguishable from wild type, and E50K-overexpressing retinal cells show an increased early apoptotic fraction.

evidence.snippet: All 11 subjects had normal tension glaucoma (NTG), with presenting and highest IOP of 15.3 +/- 3.0 and 16.5 +/- 2.5 mm Hg (+/-SD) on diurnal testing.
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the normal intraocular pressures at which the optic neuropathy occurs in E50K carriers, which is the defining claim of this node.

evidence.snippet: The rate of filtration surgery performed for progressive visual field loss in those with and without the E50K mutation was 72.7% and 25.3%, respectively (P = 0.003), and all subjects with E50K were found to have progressing visual fields.
evidence.explanation: Supports the more aggressive course relative to mutation-negative normal-tension glaucoma asserted in this node.

evidence.snippet: The optineurin (OPTN) E50K mutation was first identified in familial primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG), the onset of which is not associated with intraocular pressure (IOP) elevation, and is classified as normal-tension glaucoma (NTG).
evidence.explanation: States the IOP-independence of onset that separates this node from the module's elevated-IOP arm.

evidence.snippet: Common features of OPTN -associated NTG due to Glu50Lys mutation included early onset of disease with an IOP <21 mm Hg, marked optic disc cupping, and progressive visual field loss
evidence.explanation: Independent long-follow-up pedigree series describing the same clinical triad of early onset, sub-21 mmHg IOP, marked cupping and progressive field loss.

steps/7.description: Cumulative ganglion cell and axon loss produces the clinical entity: deep optic disc cupping, retinal nerve fibre layer thinning, and progressive visual field loss, with an open and unremarkable drainage angle and intraocular pressures at or below 21 mmHg. The defining feature relative to the rest of the glaucoma family is that this endpoint is reached without the elevated-IOP step: E50K carriers in the Moorfields series had mean presenting and peak diurnal IOP of about 15 and 17 mmHg, and E50K mice develop retinal degeneration at intraocular pressures statistically indistinguishable from wild-type littermates. Relative to mutation-negative normal-tension glaucoma the course is more aggressive - younger age at presentation, deeper cupping and smaller rim area at diagnosis, and a much higher rate of filtration surgery for progressive field loss.

evidence.snippet: A glaucoma-associated mutant of optineurin, E50K, impairs autophagy as well as vesicle trafficking, leading to death of retinal cells by apoptosis.
evidence.explanation: States the E50K-to-impaired-autophagy step that this edge asserts. Evidence source is OTHER because this is a review; the cell work it summarises is reported in the primary papers it cites. Note also that the sentence says "retinal cells", not retinal ganglion cells specifically.

edges/2.description: The misfolded, TBK1-bound mutant protein is itself the autophagy receptor, so its aberrant state directly disables the flux it should support.

evidence.snippet: At the molecular level, introduction of the E50K mutation disrupts the interaction between Optn and Rab8 GTPase, a protein involved in the regulation of vesicle transport from Golgi to plasma membrane.
evidence.explanation: Directly evidences the E50K-to-Rab8-disruption step that this edge asserts.

edges/3.description: The same substitution abolishes the optineurin-Rab8 interaction that supports Golgi-to-membrane vesicle transport.

evidence.snippet: It is involved in xenophagy, mitophagy, aggrephagy, and tumor suppression.
evidence.explanation: Places mitophagy among the optineurin-dependent selective-autophagy programmes, which is what makes this edge follow. Evidence source is OTHER because this is a review.

edges/4.description: Mitophagy is one of the selective-autophagy programmes optineurin serves, so a receptor-level lesion propagates into it.

evidence.snippet: Thus, an optimum level of optineurin-mediated autophagy is crucial for survival of retinal cells, and impaired autophagy is likely to contribute to glaucoma pathogenesis.
evidence.explanation: States the autophagy-to-retinal-cell-survival dependency that this edge asserts. Evidence source is OTHER because this is a review.

evidence.snippet: Moreover, rapamycin increased the RGC number and visual function of E50K mice.
evidence.explanation: Rescue by an autophagy inducer, the intervention evidence that the flux block is causal for ganglion cell loss rather than a bystander.

edges/5.description: Loss of autophagic quality control in a long-lived post-mitotic neuron leads to its apoptotic death; forcing flux rescues the phenotype, which is what makes this edge causal rather than correlative.

evidence.snippet: Glaucoma-associated mutants of OPTN, E50K, and M98K, cause defective vesicle trafficking, autophagy, and signaling that contribute to death of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs).
evidence.explanation: Graded PARTIAL: the review supports autophagy-family defects contributing to ganglion cell death but does not isolate the mitophagy arm specifically, which is why this node is curated as an amplifier. Evidence source is OTHER because this is a review.

edges/6.description: Accumulation of damaged mitochondria in an energetically demanding neuron with long unmyelinated intraretinal axons contributes to its death.

evidence.snippet: Glaucoma-associated mutants of OPTN, E50K, and M98K, cause defective vesicle trafficking, autophagy, and signaling that contribute to death of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs).
evidence.explanation: Graded INDIRECT: the review bundles trafficking with autophagy and signalling as joint contributors and does not establish an independent trafficking-to-apoptosis route. Evidence source is OTHER because this is a review.

edges/7.description: Trafficking failure is reported as a contributor to ganglion cell death, but the intermediate steps between disturbed vesicle transport and apoptosis are not established, hence an indirect edge.

evidence.snippet: After 16 months, histological abnormalities were exclusively observed in the retina of E50K mutant mice with loss of RGCs and connecting synapses in the peripheral retina leading to a thinning of the nerve fiber layer at the optic nerve head at normal IOP.
evidence.explanation: Explicitly links ganglion cell loss to nerve fibre layer thinning at the optic nerve head, the structural endpoint of this edge, and does so at normal intraocular pressure.

edges/8.description: Cumulative ganglion cell and axon loss is what produces the cupping, nerve fibre layer thinning and field loss that define the clinical entity.

evidence.snippet: Sequence alterations in OPTN were found in 16.7% of families with hereditary POAG, including individuals with normal intraocular pressure.
evidence.explanation: Establishes OPTN sequence alterations as the cause in a defined fraction of hereditary POAG families, including normal-pressure cases.

evidence.snippet: Optineurin is expressed in trabecular meshwork, nonpigmented ciliary epithelium, retina, and brain, and we speculate that it plays a neuroprotective role.
evidence.explanation: Documents the retinal expression that makes a ganglion-cell-autonomous mechanism plausible, and the originally proposed neuroprotective role.

evidence.snippet: Glaucoma-associated mutations of OPTN are mostly missense mutations.
evidence.explanation: Supports the statement that the glaucoma-causing OPTN allele class is predominantly missense. Evidence source is OTHER because this is a review article.

genes/0.notes:
OPTN (optineurin) at the GLC1E locus on 10p14 is the causative gene for this entity. Glaucoma-associated OPTN changes are predominantly missense; the recurrent p.Glu50Lys (E50K) allele segregates with disease in large pedigrees and accounts for essentially all of the well-characterized mechanistic work. It is a heterozygous germline change acting by toxic gain of function rather than by haploinsufficiency - the mutant protein acquires abnormal TBK1 binding, insolubility and covalent cross-linking rather than merely losing wild-type activity - which is consistent with the dominant inheritance. Optineurin is expressed in retina as well as in trabecular meshwork and nonpigmented ciliary epithelium, but the disease-relevant lesion in this entity is the retinal one.
The related Mendelian normal-tension glaucoma gene TBK1 is not curated as a gene of this entity. TBK1 copy-number gain causes its own normal-tension glaucoma and belongs to a separate disease concept; TBK1 appears here only as the interacting kinase through which mutant optineurin acts, and as a drug target.

evidence.snippet: The frequency of the missense Met98Lys variant was higher in the POAG and NTG groups than in the control group (16.9% versus 5%, 15.4% versus 5%; P = 0.009 and P = 0.029, and odds ratio 3.85 and 3.45, respectively, for the dominant effect of the OPTN A allele).
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the association of M98K with POAG and NTG in a Japanese case-control series, supporting the SUSCEPTIBILITY typing.

evidence.snippet: A polymorphism of optineurin, M98K, associated with glaucoma, causes enhanced autophagy leading to transferrin receptor degradation and apoptotic death of retinal cells.
evidence.explanation: Supports the claim that M98K acts through enhanced rather than impaired autophagy, the opposite direction to E50K. Evidence source is OTHER because this is a review.

evidence.snippet: subsequent studies have revealed that M98K polymorphism is associated with glaucoma in Asian populations but not in Caucasian populations
evidence.explanation: Directly supports the non-replication statement in this block's features text: the M98K association holds in Asian but not Caucasian cohorts. Evidence source is OTHER because this is a review article.

evidence.snippet: In some populations, generally Caucasian cohorts, the frequency of this mutation is similar among NTG patients and controls
evidence.explanation: States the case-control finding behind the non-replication claim - in Caucasian cohorts M98K frequency does not differ between NTG patients and controls.

genes/1.notes: The population-specificity of this association cuts both ways and is recorded as an open discussion below: the Caucasian-derived causative alleles were themselves absent from Japanese glaucoma cohorts.

evidence.snippet: progressive visual field loss which appeared to stabilize once an IOP of less than 10 mm Hg was achieved
evidence.explanation: The observation behind the very low target pressure recommended for OPTN-related normal-tension glaucoma.

evidence.snippet: Betaxolol, brimonidine, prostaglandin analogues, trabeculectomy (in refractory cases), systemic calcium channel blockers (such as nifedipine) and 24-hour monitoring of blood pressure are considered in the management of NTG.
evidence.explanation: Source for the agent classes bound in therapeutic_agent. Graded PARTIAL and tagged OTHER deliberately: this is a narrative review of normal-tension glaucoma in general, NOT of OPTN-related disease, so it establishes what is used in NTG management and not that any of these agents has OPTN-specific evidence. Calcium channel blockers are named in the quote but deliberately not bound as agents here - they target the vascular-dysregulation model of non-Mendelian NTG, which is not this entity's mechanism.

evidence.snippet: Treatment is generally aimed to lower IOP by 30% from pre-existing levels to 12-14 mmHg.
evidence.explanation: The general NTG pressure target, for contrast with the sub-10 mmHg target the OPTN-specific pedigree evidence above supports. Graded PARTIAL because it is a general-NTG figure, not an OPTN-specific one.

treatments/0.description: All established glaucoma therapy works by lowering intraocular pressure, and that remains the only evidence-based intervention for OPTN-related disease even though the pressure is not elevated to begin with. In a four-generation Glu50Lys pedigree followed for a mean of 17 years, visual field progression appeared to stabilize only once IOP was brought below 10 mmHg, so the target pressure is substantially lower than in ordinary open-angle glaucoma. This is an observational pedigree finding, not a randomized result.

evidence.snippet: The rate of filtration surgery performed for progressive visual field loss in those with and without the E50K mutation was 72.7% and 25.3%, respectively (P = 0.003)
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the excess rate of filtration surgery in E50K carriers.

treatments/1.description: Filtering surgery for progressive visual field loss is required far more often in E50K carriers than in mutation-negative normal-tension glaucoma (72.7% versus 25.3% in the Moorfields series). This reflects the aggressive natural history rather than a mutation-specific surgical indication.
